summary: Mission Architect is a free web game that turns real space mission design into something anyone can play. Players choose a destination, a launch vehicle and spacecraft modules, balancing mass, power, budget and delta-v with the real rocket equation, then fly the mission through event cards to a scored debrief. It helps students and space fans feel the real trade-offs mission engineers face, using genuine NASA data throughout.
details:
Mission Architect is a web-based game where you design, build and fly your own space mission. The player picks a difficulty, chooses a destination — the Moon, Mars or asteroid Bennu — selects a launch vehicle, and then builds a spacecraft module by module in the mission builder. Every choice is a real engineering trade-off: the game continuously tracks mass, power, budget and delta-v using the real Tsiolkovsky rocket equation, and a design that is overweight, underpowered or short on delta-v is blocked at launch with the reasons explained in plain language. Valid designs fly through a simulation of event cards — radiation, space weather and system events drawn from real data — and every mission ends with a score, a grade and a personalised debrief.

All of the numbers in the game come from genuine NASA data, simplified for players but never invented: planetary data from the NASA Planetary Fact Sheets (NSSDC), radiation data from the NASA Open Science Data Repository (OSDR, including RadLab), asteroid data for Bennu from the NASA JPL Small-Body Database, and space weather data from NASA DONKI via api.nasa.gov.

The goal is to let students and space fans feel the real constraints mission engineers work under — that every kilogram, watt and dollar spent on one system is taken from another — in a game that runs free in any browser, with no install and no sign-up.

Built with React, TypeScript, Vite and Tailwind CSS. Live game: https://missionarchitect.netlify.app — source code: https://github.com/twsf-strugg1es/mission-architect
